text: In what order should Milestone 3 be built?

options.label: Platform (harness, rules modules, CI gate, timer), then map and battle (sub-regions, d20), then economy, then content
options.rationale: Measure before changing balance; sub-regions are the floor that cities, income, and supply stand on.

options.label: Economy first, as the old milestone3.md draft planned, with the harness alongside
d20 and unit types first, economy and map later
All ideas in parallel streams from the start
The four-revision cut on this page: rail, movement points, more unit types, and support orders wait
options.rationale: Delivers the economy on a finer map while staying near the 6/10 complexity target.

options.label: Smaller: revisions 1 to 3 only (platform, map and battle, economy); weather, artillery, and exhaustion move to Milestone 4
Smallest: the old draft's scope (income, recruitment, replenishment) plus the harness; no sub-regions or d20 yet
Larger: also rail and air units in Milestone 3

text: What should a harness run decide at each Milestone 3 merge?

options.label: A gate with explicit budgets the owner sets (freeze rate, minimum share per faction), checked with intervals on paired seeds
options.rationale: Turns balance from a report into a decision, without tuning by hand.

options.label: Measure and report only, as P3 did in Milestone 2
Set budgets only for the end of Milestone 3, not per merge

text: Which graded results take a whole territory rather than some of its sub-regions?

options.label: The Military ladder as proposed: the four best grades take all, two grades flip 1 or 2 sub-regions
options.rationale: Keeps today's chance to take a territory per odds column, so harness runs compare cleanly with Milestone 2.

options.label: Only the best grade takes all; the middle grades flip 1, 2, or 3 sub-regions (more partitions, slower conquest)
Ground as a share of the territory (a quarter, a half, all), so large and small territories behave alike
Let the harness choose between these on freeze rate and partition frequency

text: How do factions fight inside a territory they share?

options.label: Keep M27 standing battles, fought once a turn per territory, and let their ground grade flip sub-regions
options.rationale: No new order type and already tested; the ladder gives it the partial results it lacked.

options.label: Replace M27 with an explicit Push order from one sub-region into a neighbouring enemy sub-region (the Map cluster's design)
Keep M27 now and add Push when sub-regions become the movement grid

text: How should orders that are not moves (Replenish, Recruit, builds, air missions) be submitted?

options.label: Armies get an order union (Move or Replenish, with Entrench and Rest still derived); Recruit and builds go in a separate per-faction purchase list
options.rationale: Keeps one order per army and puts site-based purchases where they belong, in one contract change.

options.label: One flat list of typed orders per faction, armies and sites alike
Keep submissions as moves only; economic choices are made in a separate step after resolution

text: How long is a turn, and how long is a game?

options.label: Two weeks per turn, stored in a scenario calendar block; the harness also runs 60 to 70 turns to reach the first winters and Teruel
options.rationale: Every cluster already assumed two weeks; weather and aid schedules need real dates.

options.label: One month per turn, so 30 turns covers about two and a half years
Two weeks per turn, with a turn limit and a cities-held result to end long games
Keep game length open until the harness shows how long games run
